findings.current: ↑↓ mover · space seleccionar · a todas/ninguna · enter vista previa · esc volver
findings.english: ↑↓ move · space select · a all/none · enter preview · esc back
findings.problem: The assembled sessions-state hint row is 80 cells against the 76-cell row the view documents at 80x24 ('The hint row still fits at 80x24 (76 cells)'), and show_move keeps all five hints at width >= 74, so nothing sheds. The row cannot fit and the trailing hint (esc volver, the way out) is clipped on the screen's main state. English fits at 62.
findings.suggested: ↑↓ mover · space elegir · a todas/ninguna · enter vista previa · esc volver
findings.alternative: ↑↓ mover · space seleccionar · a todo/nada · enter vista previa · esc volver (76 cells, exactly at the limit)

findings.problem: Every other hint label is an infinitive (volver, cancelar, confirmar, importar, mover, abrir, recargar, seleccionar), matching the guide's action-label rule and shipped tui.viewer precedent ('r recargar · o abrir externamente · esc cerrar'). 'lista' names a thing. In the result state it is painted beside 'esc volver', so one row reads noun + verb. hint_preview ('vista previa') has the same shape but is not flagged: the preview noun is used consistently across this catalogue, so it reads as the screen, not as a broken label.

findings.note: identifier corrected in finding body below
findings.current: Selecciona al menos una sesión con espacio antes de previsualizar.
findings.english: Select at least one session with space before previewing.
findings.problem: 'con espacio' reads first as 'with room' in Spanish; the referent is the space bar (the hint row names it 'space'). This is the message a blocked user uses to unblock themselves, so ambiguity costs a failed attempt.
findings.suggested: Selecciona al menos una sesión con la tecla espacio antes de previsualizar.

findings.problem: 'ocultados' reads as 'hidden ones'; what happened is content scrubbed for safety, which Spanish expresses as 'censurados' or 'redactados'. The count and the fact are right, so this is wording, not a misstatement.

preview_narrow renders the same fact as '{count} seleccionadas', so one screen shows two shapes; and the count sits last, where _detail_text's truncate_cells would eat it, while the English leads with the number.

findings.current: Puede que el harness haya eliminado el rollout.
findings.english: The harness may have removed the rollout.
findings.problem: 'rollout' is the Codex artefact's own name and is correctly kept as a machine term, but a Spanish reader outside Codex must decode it from context. Recorded, not required to change.
findings.suggested: leave as is, or 'el volcado de sesión'
